We now extend to **multiple linear regression** with $p$ predictors:

$$
\hat{y}_i = \hat{b}_0 + \hat{b}_1 x_{1i} + \hat{b}_2 x_{2i} + ... + \hat{b}_p x_{2p}
$$

### Question 3

Suppose we are building a linear model to predict **penguin bill depth (mm)** using: $x_1$: flipper length (mm) and $x_2$: body mass (g). Why might using more than one predictor improve predictions?


\newpage

## Multiple predictors

Suppose we fit this model A:
$$
\widehat{\text{Bill Depth}}_i = 35.5 -0.1 \times\text{Flipper Length}_i + 0.0004 \times \text{Body Mass}_i
$$

## Categorical predictors

Now suppose we extend our model by including species as a predictor. Model B: 
\begin{equation*}
  \begin{split}
    \widehat{\text{Bill Depth}}_i = &7.7 + 0.3 \times\text{Flipper Length}_i + 0.001 \times \text{Body Mass}_i\\
    &- 0.2\times I (\text{Species}_i = \text{Chinstrap}) - 5.9\times I (\text{Species}_i = \text{Gentoo})
  \end{split}
\end{equation*}

## Evaluating models

```{r}
#| echo: false

round_digits <- 2

set.seed(234)

penguins_split <- rsample::initial_split(penguins, prop = 0.75) # 75% to 25% split
penguins_train_data <- rsample::training(penguins_split)
penguins_test_data <- rsample::testing(penguins_split)

model_z <- model_4_train <- lm(
  bill_dep ~ flipper_len,  
  data = penguins_train_data
)

model_a <- model_4_train <- lm(
  bill_dep ~ flipper_len + body_mass,  
  data = penguins_train_data
)

model_b <- model_4_train <- lm(
  bill_dep ~ flipper_len + body_mass + species,  
  data = penguins_train_data
)

model_evals <- data.frame(
  model = c("Z", "A", "B"),
  train_r_squared = c(
    broom::glance(model_z)$r.squared,
    broom::glance(model_a)$r.squared,
    broom::glance(model_b)$r.squared
  ),
  train_adj_r_squared = c(
    broom::glance(model_z)$adj.r.squared,
    broom::glance(model_a)$adj.r.squared,
    broom::glance(model_b)$adj.r.squared
  ),
  test_rmse = c(
    modelr::rmse(model_z, data = penguins_test_data),
    modelr::rmse(model_a, data = penguins_test_data),
    modelr::rmse(model_b, data = penguins_test_data)
  )
) |> 
  mutate(
    train_r_squared = round(train_r_squared, digits = round_digits),
    train_adj_r_squared = round(train_adj_r_squared, digits = round_digits),
    test_rmse = round(test_rmse, digits = round_digits)
  )
```

Consider the three following models:

| Model | Predictors | R² (train) | Adjusted R² (train) | RMSE (test)
|------|-----------|----|-------------|--------------|
| Z | Flipper length | `r filter(model_evals, model == "Z") |> pull(train_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "Z") |> pull(train_adj_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "Z") |> pull(test_rmse)` |
| A | Flipper + Body mass | `r filter(model_evals, model == "A") |> pull(train_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "A") |> pull(train_adj_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "A") |> pull(test_rmse)` |
| B | Flipper + Body mass + Species | `r filter(model_evals, model == "B") |> pull(train_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "B") |> pull(train_adj_r_squared)` | `r filter(model_evals, model == "B") |> pull(test_rmse)` |
